Biman signs Airbus deal to acquire ten aircraft
item.description:
Biman Bangladesh Airlines today signed an agreement with Airbus to acquire 10 aircraft, taking its planned acquisition pipeline to 35 jets as the national flag carrier seeks to expand capacity and strengthen its market share.

The agreement covers four A350-900 wide-body aircraft and six A321neo narrow-body jets to support Biman''s long-haul and regional network expansion.

Airbus India and South Asia President and Managing Director Jürgen Westermeier and Biman Board Chairman Rumee A Hossain signed the agreement on behalf of their respective sides.

Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir witnessed the signing at Radisson Blu Dhaka Water Garden here this evening.

Speaking at the ceremony, Millat said the Airbus acquisition formed part of the government's plan to expand Biman, which currently accounts for only about 20 percent of Bangladesh's air passenger market.

He said the fleet expansion would help the national carrier increase its capacity and capture a greater share of the market.

Humaiun Kobir said Bangladesh was purchasing aircraft from Europe and the United States to meet its own requirements, rather than to please any country.

The procurement decisions reflected Bangladesh's aviation needs and plans for the national carrier''s expansion, he said.

The aircraft deliveries are expected to begin in 2030, although Millat requested that some aircraft be delivered ahead of schedule.

The ceremony, titled "Spreading Our Wings Together", was also attended by Invest Bangladesh Executive Chairman Ashik Chowdhury. Ambassadors of the European Union, France, the United Kingdom, Spain and Germany also spoke.

Biman Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Kaizer Sohel Ahmed delivered the welcome address.

Hossain said the inclusion of Airbus aircraft was part of Biman''s long-term vision to build a sustainable mixed fleet.

He described the expansion as a major but reasonable ambition, noting that Bangladesh handles more than 15 million air passengers annually.The wide-body aircraft would serve routes to the Middle East, Europe, North America and Australia, while the narrow-body jets would focus on regional destinations and medium-haul Asian hubs, he said.

The signing followed months of evaluation and negotiations during which Biman and Airbus reached agreement on outstanding issues.

It comes shortly after Biman expanded its Boeing acquisition programme to 25 aircraft through two agreements signed this year.

The first agreement, signed on 30 April, covered 14 Boeing aircraft worth US$3.7 billion, comprising eight 787-10 Dreamliners, two 787-9 Dreamliners and four 737-8 jets.

A supplementary agreement signed in New York on September 23 added five 787-10 Dreamliners and six 737-8 aircraft under a provision allowing the purchase of additional aircraft.

Millat said the additional 11 Boeing aircraft would cost about USD 2.7 billion, based on the rates agreed under the April contract.

Together, the Boeing and Airbus agreements cover 35 aircraft, comprising 19 wide-body and 16 narrow-body jets.

Boeing deliveries are scheduled to begin in November 2031 and continue through 2035. Bangladesh has requested earlier delivery of at least one aircraft, possibly in 2027 or 2028, the minister said.

Biman currently operates 19 aircraft, with Boeing dominating its fleet. The Airbus acquisition would introduce a broader mixed fleet as the airline expands its network.

item.title: Where will we keep so many aircraft?
item.description:
I'm afraid to question about buying airplanes! It's not an easy task to determine which questions are acceptable and which ones are not. Our current government came to power just eight months ago. In that short time, it has either completed or is in the process of completing agreements to purchase 35 aircraft. The first question that came to my mind after reading the news is, where are we going to keep so many airplanes?

There are more questions tumbling around in my head—do we have the infrastructure to operate such a large fleet? What are the terms under which these planes are being purchased? Where will the financing for the purchase come from? If, for some reason, we need to back out of the agreement, is there an option to do so in the contract? If there is, will there be a penalty?

The aviation minister has said that it will cost $6. 4 billion (approximately Tk 787 billion) to purchase 25 Boeing aircraft as per the agreement. Of course, these planes will be delivered in phases, and payments will be made at the time of delivery; the first is expected in 2031, and the final one in 2035. This means that the financing and delivery timeline extends beyond the current government's term and could become a burden for the next government.

There are more questions. The government is only eight months old; when did it find the time for planning and negotiating these aircraft purchases? Has there been any due diligence to ensure the precise implementation skills necessary for buying and operating so many planes?

Many might say, "Why does an 'outsider' need to know so much about airplanes?” However, these days, the general public seems to have a heightened interest in everything—students are making governments, 'cockroaches' are doing politics, and 'outsiders' are getting updates on airplanes instead of ships!

People haven't overlooked one aspect of buying airplanes. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has talked about purchasing aircraft from the US's Boeing! Two days later, information about buying planes from Europe's Airbus came from the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism.

A question frequently heard from everyone about buying airplanes is—has the US forced 25 Boeing planes upon us? But the biggest question is, given Bangladesh Airlines' track record, will it be possible for the airline to operate so many airplanes efficiently and run a profitable business? What does Biman Bangladesh's track record look like?

Skytrax is an international agency that reviews the operations of various airlines worldwide and prepares a report each year. According to the Skytrax report, Biman Bangladesh Airlines has a rating of three out of five.

In other words, Biman is a three-star airline. This rating is determined based on the standards of the domestic airports, the quality of the materials used by the airline (such as seating quality), other facilities, and cleanliness. One of the major factors in the rating is the quality and efficiency of the cabin crew and other staff.

Work on the third terminal of Dhaka Airport began seven years ago and is still ongoing. Dhaka Airport has only one runway, meaning no more than one aircraft can land simultaneously. The plan to add another runway remains confined to paper.

In the Skytrax report on Biman’s operations, it mentions, "The airline has a lot of inconsistencies that impact its ratings. More focus is needed on cleanliness and cabin maintenance. The service from the cabin crew ranges from good to quite poor, and there’s a need for improvement in consistency here. The service quality at Dhaka airport is still very weak. ”

However, Biman has received a five-star rating concerning safety, as there have been no major accidents in the past 40 years. This is a major positive aspect for Biman. Yet it can be said with certainty that if Biman does not make significant changes in its operations, then merely expanding its fleet with large planes will not increase its profitability, service, or reputation.

The former Chairman of the Bangladesh Civil Aviation Authority (CAAB), Air Vice Marshal (retd.) Mahmud Hossain, recently said at a discussion, “The biggest crisis in Bangladesh's aviation sector is not aircraft but the deficiency of skilled manpower. Despite increasing demand, there is a shortage of pilots and licenced aircraft maintenance engineers in the country.”

On paper, Biman Bangladesh appears to be a highly profitable organisation. It has reported an annual profit of Tk 9.37 billion for the fiscal year 2024-25, which is a record in Biman’s history. However, beneath this apparent glow lies a significant shadow.

Major questions have been raised on social media and in the news about these earnings, suggesting that Biman is actually a loss-making entity; because it has over Tk 81 billion in unpaid debts owed to various government agencies.

What is the future plan after buying so many planes? Although not very clear, some signs of government thought processes can be gleaned from ministers’ statements. Some envision building a 'travel hub' in Dhaka, while others aspire to build a large fleet like Ethiopian Airlines and make a significant contribution to the country’s GDP.

Many questions will arise from these issues. Our country’s tourism facilities are woefully inadequate, the condition of airports is shamefully poor, and there is a lack of skilled manpower for airline operations. Without significant changes in these areas, building a ‘hub’ will remain a far-fetched dream. Moreover, due to the war in the Middle East, there are concerns about maintaining job markets for our workers there. Amidst this, a significant number of workers have returned home. The question arises, will this impact constrict air travel in Bangladesh?

Comparing with Ethiopian Airlines also doesn’t bring much confidence. It’s a four-star airline. According to Skytrax, Ethiopian Airlines is a highly disciplined organisation that has increased its profits annually and gradually procured new airplanes. In comparison, here everything other than the airplane purchase agreements is progressing at a snail's pace.
Work on the third terminal of Dhaka Airport began seven years ago and is still ongoing. Dhaka Airport has only one runway, meaning no more than one aircraft can land simultaneously. The plan to add another runway remains confined to paper.

Considering all of this, it seems that hastily signing contracts to purchase new airplanes is a huge risk. Many will question whether such an extensive buying plan was made with careful planning and profit-loss considerations.

However, it is also true that since the agreements to purchase the planes have been or need to be made, optimism is the best course. No matter what arguments or questions anyone may have, we all hope that Biman Bangladesh can elevate our travel industry to a higher, more disciplined level!

item.description:
Dinesh Trivedi, the Indian High Commissioner stationed in Bangladesh, met with India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi yesterday, Tuesday afternoon, in New Delhi.

Diplomatic sources have said that, in addition to matters concerning the relationship between the two neighbouring countries, there was also a discussion between Narendra Modi and Dinesh Trivedi regarding the current position of Dhaka on the possible visit of Bangladesh's Prime Minister, Tarique Rahman, to India.

Dinesh Trivedi arrived in New Delhi from Dhaka on Monday night and met with Narendra Modi on Tuesday afternoon.

Moreover, the country's High Commissioner in Dhaka met with India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri.

Dhaka's diplomatic sources have reported that Dinesh Trivedi is expected to return to Dhaka next Thursday.

In August, Dinesh Trivedi went to New Delhi and held a meeting with Narendra Modi.

At that time, he also discussed with the India's Prime Minister about the possible visit of Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

However, nothing has been officially communicated by India regarding the discussion this time.

Yesterday, India's High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi also met with the country's Army Chief, General Dhiraj Seth.

The meeting discussed various aspects of strengthening bilateral cooperation and defence relations between Bangladesh and India.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,140 as six die in 24 hours
item.description:
Six more children have died from measles and measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,140.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified four of the latest casualties as suspected and two as confirmed measles deaths.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,036, while the number of confirmed deaths rose to 104.
Among the latest fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with two suspected and two confirmed deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 1,280 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 200,293.
During the same period, 110 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 22,020.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 177,676 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 170,473 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Gazi Nazrul’s bail plea rejected in second wife’s death case
item.description:
A Dhaka court has rejected the bail petition of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam in a case filed over the alleged abetment of the suicide of his second wife, Mariyam Akter.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam passed the order after a hearing on Wednesday.
State counsel Harun-or-Rashid confirmed the matter.
Defence lawyers Mahbubur Rahman, Mizanur Rahman and others sought bail for Gazi Nazrul, while the prosecution opposed the petition.
The defence argued that Gazi Nazrul was innocent and had no involvement in the incident. They said he was named in the case to harass him and that police arrested him on September 20 after calling him to the police station for questioning.
They also said police had failed to produce any evidence of abetment of suicide despite questioning him during remand.
The bail petition said the complainant and the accused were relatives and had reached a settlement through family discussions. It said Gazi Nazrul, 75, is a veteran politician and freedom fighter who suffers from a serious heart condition. The defence also argued that he has a permanent address and would not go into hiding or leave the country if granted bail.
The complainant’s lawyers also submitted a settlement agreement to the court.
In the agreement, Mariyam’s father said he had initially filed the case against Gazi Nazrul, his first wife Maksuda Islam and Mariyam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman based on his immediate suspicion following his daughter’s death.
He later concluded, after family discussions and considering other information, that Mariyam had not died by suicide at the instigation of Gazi Nazrul or Maksuda. He said he had no objection to the accused being released on bail.
However, state counsel Harun-or-Rashid told the court that the case was not compoundable despite the settlement.
He said the investigation was ongoing and would determine the facts, including whether Mariyam died by suicide or was killed.
The state counsel also said further information could emerge if Obaidur Rahman was arrested and questioned.
Earlier, on September 30, a court granted bail to Gazi Nazrul’s first wife, Maksuda Islam, in the case.
On September 20, police recovered the hanging body of Mariyam Akter from a flat at NAM Bhaban opposite the Parliament complex. Police later took Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda into custody.
That night, Mariyam’s father, SM Masum Billah, filed the case against Gazi Nazrul, Maksuda and Obaidur, accusing them of abetting her suicide.
The following day, a court granted Gazi Nazrul four days’ remand and Maksuda one day’s remand following a petition by Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police Sub-Inspector Md Shamsuzzoha Sarker.
The case was handed over to the Detective Branch that night.
On September 23, a court ordered Obaidur, who had been arrested in the case, to be sent to jail.

item.title: Rajbari’s ilish glory fades as Padma loses depth, current
item.description:
The boats are still there; the nets are still there. But the ilish that once filled the fishing boats on the Padma River in Rajbari has largely disappeared.
Along the riverbank at Bahir Char Daulatdia in Goalanda, rows of fishing boats remain moored. Some fishermen return from the river with their meagre catch, while others sit in their boats repairing torn nets or applying tar to fishing gear under the sun.
For fisherman Shukur Ali Haldar, 75, the scene is a painful reminder of a very different Padma.
“I have been fishing in the Padma for nearly 50 years. We used to get five to seven maunds of ilish in a single haul. Sometimes the nets were so heavy with fish that we could hardly pull them up. We would return to the ghat with boats full of ilish,” he said.
“Now the Padma has neither the depth nor the current it once had. Because of the loss of depth, ilish are no longer found here like before,” he said.
In the past, the river would come alive after dusk with the flickering lights of fishing boats and fishermen would cast their nets throughout the night and return at dawn with boats loaded with fish, he added.
Goalanda’s importance as an ilish landing and trading centre was closely linked to its location at the confluence of the Padma and Jamuna rivers.
During the British period and for years after partition, large quantities of ilish caught in the area were transported by rail to Kolkata.
Local traders said ilish from Goalanda was once shipped in railway wagons to different parts of the region.
But the river has changed over the decades.
Submerged chars have emerged in many places, reducing navigability and altering the river’s flow.
Fishermen said the decline in depth and current, combined with changes in fishing practices and other environmental pressures, has contributed to the disappearance of ilish from the Rajbari stretch of the Padma.
Haldar said he had also witnessed the decline over the years.
“I have caught ilish with fishermen such as Zafar Haldar, Sonai Haldar, Niranjan Haldar and Madan Haldar of Jafarganj in Manikganj. We used to catch two- to three-seer ilish regularly,” he said.
He recalled selling a roughly one-kilogram ilish for Tk 3,600 during the peak season in one year.
But the situation changed after major floods, he said.
“Ilish started declining after the 1988 flood. After the 1998 flood, ilish almost disappeared from the Padma,” he said.
Osel Bepari, former general secretary of the Daulatdia-Debagram Fishermen’s Cooperative Society, said fishermen from Rajbari as well as Manikganj, Sirajganj and Pabna used to come to this stretch of the river.
He said around 40 local boats, 12 boats from Manikganj and 16 from Sirajganj and Pabna were once engaged in fishing in the area. This year, only around 27 local boats are operating, he said.
He said fishermen now have to travel far downstream to find suitable fishing grounds. A boat may get only one opportunity to cast and retrieve its net every 16 to 17 hours.
“With ilish becoming scarce, fishermen are increasingly using different types of nets to catch whatever fish they can find,” he said.
Anwar Bepari, 65, who has spent about four decades fishing in the river, recalled a time when a boat could catch 50 to 60 maunds of ilish a day.“Now you can hardly say there is fish in the Padma.”
He blamed the use of illegal current nets and China-duari nets for destroying fish and their eggs, while also pointing to changes in the river caused by upstream structures and the formation of chars.
“The river no longer has enough water or current,” he said.
Fish traders and wholesalers around Daulatdia Ghat said their once-thriving businesses have also shrunk.
Chandu Mollah, who has been involved in the fish trade at Daulatdia ferry ghat for around 20 years, recalled seeing hundreds of kilograms of fish brought to the market every day when he started working there.
Now, he said, only a fraction of the boats return with ilish.
“At the end of the day, only 10 to 12 ilish may come from 10 to 20 boats. The fish trade has changed completely,” he said.
Badal Biswas, a wholesale ilish trader at Goalanda Bazar, has been in the business for around 35 years, following in the footsteps of his late father, Sadeq Ali Biswas.
“Business was very lively during my father’s time. ilish from Goalanda used to be sent to different parts of the country. It was even transported to Kolkata in railway wagons,” he said.
“Now there is no Padma ilish. Those days are a golden past,” Biswas said.
He has kept the family business going by bringing ilish from Barishal and Chattogram.
Mohan Mondal, president of the Daulatdia Ghat Bazar Business Association, said the decline has been dramatic even in recent years.
“Even six or seven years ago, fishermen used to bring 20 to 30 maunds of ilish to my wholesale shop every day,” he said.
There are now 11 wholesale shops at the ghat, he said, but on a recent day only two shops received ilish, totalling just 2-3 kilograms.
During the peak season, the entire ghat may receive only 10-12 kilograms in a day, Mondal said.
The decline in Rajbari is part of a broader concern over ilish production in Bangladesh.
According to the Department of Fisheries, national ilish production fell to 512,000 metric tonnes in fiscal year 2024-25 from 529,000 tonnes in 2023-24 and 571,000 tonnes in 2022-23.
Fisheries officials and researchers have also pointed to changes in river conditions and the degradation of breeding grounds as threats to the national fish.
Rajbari District Fisheries Officer Md Mahbub Ul Haque said the decline is not unique to Rajbari. Ilish production has declined across the country. Climate change is causing changes in the size and availability of ilish.”
He said the formation of numerous submerged chars has reduced river depth and navigability, while environmental changes are disrupting the fish’s normal movement.
“Human-induced pollution is also a factor. At the same time, catching mother ilish and jatka is having an impact,” he said.

item.title: Three siblings sentenced to death, 10 others get life for killing Mymensingh farmer
item.description:
A Mymensingh court on Wednesday sentenced three siblings to death and 10 others to life imprisonment for killing a farmer over a land dispute in 2015.
Judge of the Mymensingh Additional District and Sessions Judge Court-1 Shamsuddin Ahmed handed down the punishment.
The condemned convicts are Mozammel Haque Swapan Mia, 46, Apon Mia, 43, and Ripon Mia, 41-- three sons of Abu Bakar Siddique of Char Laxmidia in Nandail upazila of the district. Of them, Ripon was tried in absentia.
The lifers are Abu Bakar Siddique, 71, his son Kanchon Mia, 36, Rubel, 56, Pervez, 31, Mofazzal Hossain, 56, Kashid, 59, Al Amin, 31, Sumon Mia, 36, Noyon Mia, 29, and Ashadul, 29. Ashadul was tried in absentia.
The court also fined each of them Tk 50,000, in default to suffer one year of rigorous imprisonment.
According to the prosecution, the convicts had an enmity with Shafiqul Islam Sobi, son of Hazrat Ali of Char Bholamari area in Nandail upazila, over a piece of land.
On February 25, 2015, the convicts, equipped with local weapons, stabbed Shafiqul while he was sitting at a shop, leaving him dead on the spot.
Rafiqul Islam, brother of the deceased, filed a case with Nandail Police Station against 13 identified people and 10-12 unidentified people.
Later, police submitted chargesheet against 13 people.

item.title: Bangladesh eyes stronger tourism, fisheries cooperation with Maldives
item.description:
Underscoring the potential to expand cooperation with the Maldives in tourism and fisheries, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat urged closer collaboration to promote sustainable fisheries, develop tourism and create new avenues for bilateral engagement.
The minister made the call while speaking at a chief guest at “The Great Tuna Gala – Flavours from the Sunny Side”, organised by the Maldives High Commission to showcase the country’s sustainable tuna fishery, culinary heritage and tourism opportunities while strengthening trade, business and people-to-people ties between Bangladesh and the Maldives.
High Commissioner of Maldives to Bangladesh Shiuneen Rasheed highlighted the close connection between the Maldives and the ocean and the central place fisheries holds in the country’s economy, communities and culture.
She spoke about the Maldives’ pole-and-line tuna fishery and the importance of maintaining sustainable fishing practices, and highlighted the potential to expand Maldivian tuna and other fisheries products in the Bangladesh market.
Distinguished guests at ’The Great Tuna Gala– Flavours from the Sunny Side’ at Sheraton Dhaka, on Wednesday, October 7, 2026. Photo: Courtesy
The high commissioner also noted the growing connectivity between the two countries and the opportunities this creates for greater tourism, trade and business engagement.
The event highlighted the Maldives’ deep connection with the ocean and the important role fisheries continues to play in the country’s economy, culture and island communities.
Tuna, the mainstay of the Maldivian fisheries sector, featured prominently throughout the event, with guests introduced to a range of Maldivian fisheries products.
A particular focus was placed on the Maldives’ traditional pole-and-line fishing method, through which tuna are caught individually.
Practised in the Maldives for generations, pole-and-line fishing reflects the country’s longstanding commitment to responsible and sustainable use of its marine resources.
Renowned Maldivian Chef Maha Naseer, who travelled to Dhaka especially for the occasion, presented a live culinary demonstration featuring Maldivian dishes and showcased the versatility of tuna and other fisheries products in Maldivian cuisine.
Around 250 guests, including senior representatives of the Government of Bangladesh, members of the diplomatic corps, business leaders, tourism and fisheries industry partners, and representatives of the media, attended the event.
Guests were given an opportunity to experience authentic Maldivian flavours and learn more about the close relationship between the country’s fisheries, culinary traditions, island communities and way of life.
The Gala also showcased the Maldives as a leading global tourism destination, highlighting the country’s distinctive island experiences, natural beauty, hospitality and rich cultural heritage.
Through The Great Tuna Gala, the High Commission sought to create greater awareness of Maldivian fisheries products in Bangladesh, explore opportunities for expanding market access and business-to-business partnerships, and further promote the Maldives as a preferred destination for Bangladeshi travellers.
The event reflected the growing economic and people-to-people ties between the Maldives and Bangladesh and the potential for further cooperation in fisheries, trade, tourism and other areas of mutual interest.
The event was supported by Epitychia Holdings Pvt Ltd, VARU by Atmosphere, Maldives Industrial Fisheries Company Limited, Maldivian Airlines, Sheraton Dhaka, THE WAY DHAKA and INZAA Company Pvt Ltd.

item.title: Muhit: Dengue infection rate lower than previous years
item.description:
The dengue situation is less severe than had been feared, State Minister of Health and Family Welfare Dr MA Muhit has said.
The state minister has attributed the lower infection rate to coordinated efforts involving multiple stakeholders.
“The dengue infection rate is lower this year compared to previous years because we have taken initiatives involving everyone,” he said while visiting a vaccination session of the Special Measles-Rubella Catch-up Campaign 2026 at the Korail T&T playground in Dhaka on Wednesday.
The state minister said 20 million children across the country have already been vaccinated under the measles-rubella immunisation program. The government is working to vaccinate another 3.5 million children under the campaign over the next month.
He said the government was working to address challenges in rebuilding the country’s healthcare system.
“Under the leadership of the prime minister, healthcare for the people has been given special importance in the election campaign and manifesto. Alongside disease prevention, the health sector is also being prioritized to increase people’s productivity,” he said.
The government is prioritising the continuation of various vaccination programmes, Muhit said, adding that the US government, Gavi, Unicef, Dhaka North City Corporation and health and field-level workers across the country are supporting the efforts.
Highlighting measures taken to prevent measles, the state minister said work on the issue began after the government took office.
“Through the joint efforts of the health ministry, local government, city corporations and field-level health workers, we have already been able to vaccinate 20 million children,” he said.
He said the government had not stopped the programme after vaccinating 20 million children because “every child’s life is important.”
“The government’s goal is to ensure that not a single child is left unvaccinated. That is why this year’s programme has been taken up as a mop-up campaign,” he said.
Under the campaign, children in remote and hard-to-reach areas, children with disabilities and those who missed vaccination during earlier phases for any reason are being identified and vaccinated.
The state minister said efforts were being made to reach every child.

item.title: Shapla Chattar case: Charge framing hearing deferred to Nov 1
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal has postponed the hearing on charge framing in the case over alleged crimes against humanity committed during the Hefazat-e-Islam rally at Shapla Chattar in Motijheel, Dhaka, and set November 1 for the hearing.
International Crimes Tribunal-2 passed the order on Wednesday
The hearing had been scheduled for Wednesday, but it was postponed following an application by the prosecution.
Of the 41 accused in the case, 11 who are in custody were produced before the tribunal in the morning.
According to the prosecution, 58 people were killed in Dhaka, Narayanganj, Chittagong and Comilla in connection with the Hefazat-e-Islam rally on May 5, 2013.
The investigation agency identified 32 deaths in Dhaka, 20 in Narayanganj, five in Chittagong and one in Comilla.

item.title: Youth shot in Khulna
item.description:
A young man was shot and injured by unidentified assailants in Khulna on Wednesday morning.
The incident took place around 6:30am near the second gate of BL College under Daulatpur police station.
Police and locals said the injured man, identified as Mahidul Islam, works cleaning vehicles at an oil depot behind BL College.
He had gone to a hotel near the college’s second gate for breakfast around 6:30am when around 10 youths surrounded him and opened fire. A bullet struck him in the abdomen.
Locals took Mahidul to Khulna Medical College Hospital for treatment.
Daulatpur police station Sub-Inspector Md Abdur Razzak said police visited the scene after being informed of the incident.
“We are speaking to the injured man at the hospital to understand what happened. We are also trying to collect CCTV footage from the area,” he said.
Mahidul is the son of Shawkat Khan of Bangaon village in Muksudpur upazila of Gopalganj.
The shooting comes less than two days after Aktar Dhali was shot dead in Rupsa, further fuelling concerns over law and order in Khulna.
According to Khulna Metropolitan Police (KMP), 38 people have been killed in the city so far this year, with 23 murder cases filed.
Police said they have solved 19 of those cases and arrested 81 people.
A total of 17 cases are under investigation, and two are pending trial.
Police attributed nine killings to family or personal disputes, seven to drugs disputes, two to easy-bike theft, two to unknown causes and one to mob beating over suspicion of theft.
In 2025, at least 39 people were killed in the city and 37 murder cases were filed. Police said they solved 36 cases and arrested 144 people.
Drug dealing and turf disputes accounted for 18 of the killings, while 14 resulted from family or personal conflicts, three from attempts to steal easy-bikes and two from unknown causes.
According to Khulna District Police, 33 murder cases were filed across the district between January and September this year. Seven of the killings involved firearms.
Of the 33 cases filed across the district’s nine police stations, 11 were linked to family disputes, three to drugs, three to robbery or theft, two to turf disputes and two to financial disputes. One case involved an attack on government employees.
Police said they have solved 25 of the 33 cases.

item.title: Opposition leader Shafiqur leaves Dhaka for Turkiye
item.description:
Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer and opposition leader Dr Shafiqur Rahman left Dhaka for Turkiye on Wednesday morning to attend an international conference on Bangladesh studies.
He departed from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport for Istanbul to attend the Second International Conference on Bangladesh Studies at Istanbul University as the chief guest.
Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar, Assistant Secretary General and Central Publicity and Media Secretary Advocate Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair, and Central Executive Council Member Md Mobarak Hossain were present at the airport to see him off.
The conference, jointly organised by Istanbul University and the Center for Policy and Social Research (CPSR), will be held under the theme "Multidimensional Perspectives on Reforms in Bangladesh 2.0 and New Horizons of Turkiye-Bangladesh Cooperation."
Academics, policymakers, diplomats, researchers and representatives of various organisations and institutions from Bangladesh, Turkiye and other countries are expected to attend the conference.
After attending the conference in Turkiye, Shafiqur Rahman will travel to Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.
He is scheduled to return home on the morning of Oct 11.

item.title: Police officer seen helping drug dealer Raja escape in CCTV footage
item.description:
CCTV footage has emerged showing how Raja, alias “Picchi Raja”, a suspected drug dealer from Mohammadpur, escaped from a prison van in Dhaka, with police investigators saying an officer helped him get out of the vehicle.
Several CCTV clips obtained on Tuesday evening show the prison van stopping on a busy road in Tantibazar at around 5:58pm on September 27.
The footage shows the rear door of the van being opened as it moved slowly through traffic. Three masked people then stepped out one after another — two accused persons and a police officer.
The prison van had left a Dhaka court that evening carrying 30 accused persons to Kashimpur Jail in Gazipur.
According to the police investigation, when the van reached the area in front of Popular Diagnostic Centre in Tantibazar, it slowed down amid a traffic jam. Sub-Inspector Probir Kumar Biswas, who was in charge of the van, opened the rear door, went inside, and brought out two accused persons.
The first was Raja. The second was Khairul Bashar, owner of Cambrian School and College.
CCTV footage shows Khairul, wearing a white shirt, getting off the van and walking onto the road alongside Raja. After walking a short distance, Khairul returned to the van within seconds and took a seat beside the driver.
Raja, however, continued walking. SI Probir Kumar Biswas, wearing a red shirt, can be seen following him.
Police said Raja was allowed to leave the van so he could meet family members and subsequently escape. Khairul was allegedly allowed to sit beside the driver because the van was air-conditioned.
Investigators said the plan to help Raja escape had been made two days before the incident. The van driver and Raja’s sister, Taslima, were allegedly involved in the plan.
SI Probir Kumar Biswas, van driver Naik Kamal Hossain and Taslima have been arrested in connection with the incident.
On Tuesday, Gazipur Metropolitan Magistrate Court Judge Zubayer Rashid granted four days of remand for the three accused.
Gazipur Metropolitan Police Commissioner Israil Howlader said at a press conference on Tuesday that several other people had also been found to be involved in Raja’s escape, including a private car driver and one of his close relatives.
However, police have not yet disclosed which vehicle Raja got into after leaving the prison van or where he went.
Law enforcement agencies have increased surveillance at different points along the country’s borders in an effort to arrest him, police said.
Raja was arrested at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on May 19 while returning from Nepal with his wife and brother-in-law. He had been in jail in connection with several cases.

item.title: Inflation rises in September
item.description:
The point-to-point inflation rose to 8.34% in September 2026 from 8.26% in August.
However, the rate was slightly lower than the 8.36% recorded in September last year, according to data released by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) on Wednesday.
Food inflation increased to 7.22% in September from 7.02% in August, while non-food inflation edged down to 9.30% from 9.32%.
In September 2025, food and non-food inflation stood at 7.64% and 8.98% respectively.
At the rural level, general inflation rose to 8.38% in September from 8.31% in August, but remained below the 8.47% recorded a year earlier.
Rural food inflation increased to 7.18% in September from 7.01% in August, while non-food inflation fell slightly to 9.57% from 9.59%.
In September 2025, rural food and non-food inflation were 7.54% and 9.40% respectively.
In urban areas, general inflation increased to 8.26% in September from 8.20% in August, while it was 8.28% in September last year.
Urban food inflation rose to 7.25% in September from 7.04% in August. Non-food inflation, however, declined to 8.94% from 8.97%.
The corresponding rates in September 2025 were 7.94% for food and 8.51% for non-food items.

item.title: Software row triggers mass digital payment outage
item.description:
ATM, card, and digital transaction services across 30 banks in the country were shut down from Sunday night.
After three days, all Q-Cash services were restored late Tuesday.
Information Technology Consultants PLC (ITCL), the local payment processor operating the Q-Cash network, revealed that the crisis stemmed from a dispute over software migration between ITCL and Compass Plus, a sanctioned Russian technology firm.
ITCL stated that upon learning their platform was being replaced by "Way4"—an enterprise payment platform developed by Brussels-based OpenWay—the Russian firm injected a malicious script into ITCL's servers.
This malicious script automatically restarted ITCL's servers every eight hours.
As a result, routing tables were cleared, halting data processing capabilities across the entire network.
Kazi Saifuddin Munir, managing director and CEO of ITCL, told the media: "As soon as the issue was identified, we alerted all our partner banks, including bKash."
The dispute escalated in August when ITCL announced its decision to phase out Compass Plus's platform over a 12-to-18-month transition period.
In response, Compass Plus allegedly threatened to terminate technical support and immediately demanded a $1.5 million migration fee.
Additionally, they demanded an advance payment guarantee backed by Bangladesh Bank.
The central bank later intervened on Monday, attempting to resolve the deadlock through discussions with both the vendor firm and ITCL.
However, Bangladesh Bank officials expressed dissatisfaction with ITCL's decision to shut down the system without prior notice.
Arief Hossain Khan, executive director and spokesperson of Bangladesh Bank, stated: "This is clearly a technical issue, but the failure to manage it immediately caused severe suffering for cardholders."
Khan confirmed that the central bank will issue official show-cause notices to member banks regarding the sudden suspension of services.
Under central bank guidelines, institutions are required to notify the public well in advance through national media, television, and direct text messages before conducting any scheduled maintenance.
According to Bangladesh Bank's Payment Systems Department, ITCL's system migration was originally scheduled for late October.
The central bank on Tuesday summoned the management of ITCL, the operator of the Q-Cash network, and directed them to restore all card-related services, including switching, at the earliest possible time.
The central bank clarified that transactions for banks, Mobile Financial Services (MFS) providers, and other Payment Service Providers (PSPs) directly connected to the NPSB platform remain entirely unaffected and are functioning normally.

item.title: Pubali Bank donates bus to Comilla Victoria Govt College
item.description:

Concurrently, a tree-planting ceremony took place on the campus, and an electronic booth of the bank was inaugurated.
